concepts.name: Italian vowel and consonant pronunciation
concepts.summary: Pronounce the five pure vowels and consonants consistently, since Italian spelling is largely phonetic.

concepts.name: Hard and soft c and g
concepts.summary: Explain that c and g are soft before e and i (cena, gelato) and hard before a, o, u or with h (chi, ghetto).

concepts.name: Gn and gli sounds
concepts.summary: Recognise and produce gn as in lasagna and gli as in figlio.

concepts.name: Double consonant length
concepts.summary: Hold doubled consonants longer and understand that this changes meaning, as in pala/palla and caro/carro.

concepts.name: Greetings and politeness phrases
concepts.summary: Recall and use buongiorno, buonasera, ciao, grazie, prego, per favore and scusi in the right situations.

concepts.name: Café and restaurant ordering phrases
concepts.summary: Understand and use set phrases such as vorrei un caffè, il conto, per favore and un tavolo per due.

concepts.name: Noun gender and number
concepts.summary: Identify nouns as masculine or feminine and form regular plurals from the endings -o/-i, -a/-e and -e/-i.

misconceptions.text: Double consonants are spelled twice but pronounced like single ones.
The letter c is always pronounced like k.
Gli is pronounced like English gl in glue.

concepts.name: Definite articles il, lo, gli
concepts.summary: Choose il, lo, l', la, i, gli or le according to the gender, number and initial sound of the following word.

concepts.name: Indefinite articles un, uno, una
concepts.summary: Select un, uno, una or un' correctly depending on the following noun.

concepts.name: Essere in the present
concepts.summary: Conjugate essere and use it for identity, origin, state and description.

concepts.name: Avere in the present
concepts.summary: Conjugate avere and use it for possession and idioms such as avere fame and avere vent'anni.

concepts.name: Regular present tense verbs
concepts.summary: Conjugate regular -are, -ere and -ire verbs in the present and use them in simple sentences.

concepts.name: Adjective agreement and placement
concepts.summary: Make adjectives agree in gender and number with nouns and place them correctly, usually after the noun.

concepts.name: Articulated prepositions
concepts.summary: Combine di, a, da, in and su with definite articles, as in al bar and nel ristorante.

misconceptions.text: Il is the masculine article for every masculine noun.
Subject pronouns must always be stated, as in English.
Adjectives always come before the noun, as in English.

concepts.name: Passato prossimo formation
concepts.summary: Form the passato prossimo with the present of avere or essere plus the past participle, including irregular participles.

concepts.name: Imperfetto formation and use
concepts.summary: Form the imperfetto and use it for habits, descriptions and ongoing past actions.

concepts.name: Contrasting passato prossimo and imperfetto
concepts.summary: Analyse a narrative to decide which past tense fits completed events versus background or repeated actions.

concepts.name: Direct and indirect object pronouns
concepts.summary: Use lo, la, li, le, mi, ti, gli and le correctly, including agreement with the participle in compound tenses.

concepts.name: Choosing avere or essere auxiliary
concepts.summary: Decide between avere and essere as auxiliary, and apply participle agreement with essere.

concepts.name: Reflexive verbs
concepts.summary: Conjugate reflexive verbs and recognise that they take essere in compound tenses.

concepts.name: Future and conditional
concepts.summary: Form and use the simple future and present conditional, including polite requests such as vorrei.

misconceptions.text: Passato prossimo always takes avere as its auxiliary.
Imperfetto and passato prossimo are interchangeable and differ only in style.
The past participle never changes form.

concepts.name: Congiuntivo presente forms
concepts.summary: Form the present subjunctive of regular and common irregular verbs and recognise its endings in context.

concepts.name: Triggers for the congiuntivo
concepts.summary: Identify expressions of opinion, doubt, desire and emotion, and conjunctions like benché, that require the subjunctive.

concepts.name: Congiuntivo imperfetto and past
concepts.summary: Form and apply the imperfect and past subjunctive with correct sequence of tenses.

concepts.name: Hypothetical if-clauses
concepts.summary: Choose the right mood and tense in real, possible and unreal conditions, such as se avessi tempo, verrei.

concepts.name: Passato remoto
concepts.summary: Recognise and interpret the passato remoto in narrative and understand regional differences in its use.

concepts.name: Combined and double pronouns
concepts.summary: Combine pronouns such as glielo, me lo and ce ne and order them correctly with verbs.

concepts.name: Formal and informal register
concepts.summary: Judge when to use tu or Lei and adjust vocabulary and verb forms to the social situation.

misconceptions.text: The congiuntivo is optional and only literary, so the indicative can always replace it.
The subjunctive is used after every che clause.
The passato remoto is used everywhere in Italy instead of the passato prossimo.

concepts.name: Stylistic choice of mood and tense
concepts.summary: Evaluate when indicative or subjunctive, and which past tense, gives the intended nuance in writing and speech.

concepts.name: Regional variation and dialect influence
concepts.summary: Assess how regional Italian, dialects and standard Italian differ in pronunciation, lexicon and tense usage.

concepts.name: Idiomatic and pragmatic expression
concepts.summary: Judge the appropriateness of idioms, discourse markers and politeness strategies across contexts.

concepts.name: Complex sentence construction
concepts.summary: Compose fluent, well-structured texts that use subordination, relative clauses, and implicit forms like gerundio and infinito.

concepts.name: Register-adapted text production
concepts.summary: Create texts such as formal emails, narratives and reviews tuned to audience and purpose.

concepts.name: Error diagnosis and L1 interference
concepts.summary: Diagnose typical learner errors, including those caused by the first language, and design corrective practice.

misconceptions.text: Standard Italian is spoken uniformly across Italy.
Grammatical correctness alone guarantees natural and appropriate Italian.
Literal translation of idioms from one's own language usually yields natural Italian.
